before.description_1: There were good pieces of information on driving schools at SoDrive, but the message should have been more structured and prioritized. People should be able to scan through and understand what's in it for them, and how to proceed next easily. The wording should not be generic either.
before.description_2: As a result, I have written the text anew in such a way that each section of the page provides an answer to one specific visitor's question. In this way, my rewritten case study provides information about the driving school job opportunities in simple language and shows how their advantages will affect you in your decisions.

after.description_1: SoDrive is a driving school website built around helping learners understand lesson options, packages, the route to a licence and the next step toward starting lessons. The portfolio copy needed to describe that learner journey clearly rather than referring to job opportunities.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience around practical driving-school information, package comparison, trust signals and clear trial-lesson or contact actions. The responsive layout keeps the same decision path easy to follow for learners on mobile and desktop.

before.description_1: Boekhoudsnel needed a clearer finance page because visitors had to understand the offer before making contact. The existing story needed stronger order, more specific wording, and fewer general lines. People comparing options needed quick context, visible next steps, and enough practical detail to decide whether to continue. Before contact mattered.
before.description_2: I rebuilt the page around clearer sections, direct English copy, and practical WordPress content blocks. The structure shows what the work involves, why it matters, and how visitors can respond. Stronger scanning, calmer wording, and focused contact routes help people compare the project and make decisions with confidence. It mattered.

after.description_1: Boekhoudsnel presents bookkeeping support for entrepreneurs who want administrative work explained in practical terms. The website needed to make the service, expected support and route to contact understandable without relying on broad finance language.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress content around the bookkeeping proposition, practical questions and a clear enquiry route. The linked URL stored in ACF was malformed and could not be independently verified, so I removed that invalid value instead of replacing it with an unverified domain.

before.description_1: Regarding the energy page of Voltworks, there was a need to avoid any delay in action when the visitor was considering enquiring. The visitor would already be making comparisons, so there was a need to explain clearly what the company could do, the details involved, and what the next step was.
before.description_2: I have developed a streamlined approach to navigating the site through more concise headers and content fields in WordPress, as well as the proper wording for their projects. The design will provide better representation for Voltworks, while the visitor will be able to browse their work, discern its value, and proceed towards contacting them.

after.description_1: Voltworks presents energy solutions through a service-focused website where visitors need to understand the available technical options before requesting advice or a quotation. The content therefore needed to make the offer concrete instead of using generic language about enquiries.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience around the main energy services, supporting project information and clear contact or quotation actions. Technical detail remains available, but the first layer helps visitors identify the relevant solution and move toward a conversation.

before.description_1: Jouwgroenteboer needed a clearer ecommerce page, so visitors could understand the offer before contacting or taking action. The existing story needed more structure, more precise wording and a clearer route forward for people comparing options online.
before.description_2: I restructured the site into logical sections using plain English and WordPress content blocks. The new flow explains the offer, why it matters and what visitors can do next. Better scanning, clearer language and a defined contact path help people evaluate the project with confidence.

after.description_1: Jouwgroenteboer is an ecommerce experience for ordering fresh fruit and vegetables online. The website needed to make categories, products, delivery information and the shopping route easy to understand so customers can move from browsing to ordering without unnecessary friction.
after.description_2: I organised the WooCommerce journey around product discovery, clear category structure and direct cart actions. Supporting information stays close to the shopping flow, while the responsive layout keeps browsing and checkout practical on smaller screens.

before.description_1: Kervana needed the call to action and service offer to be clear within a few seconds. The page had to explain what the installation service includes, who it is for and why visitors should contact the business.
before.description_2: I improved the readability of the installation story with a stronger opening, clearer service sections and practical information that supports the next step. The WordPress layout makes the page easy to scan, while the copy gives visitors enough context to act confidently.

after.description_1: Kervana brings installation services such as climate, heating and related technical solutions together in one WordPress presentation. The website needed to distinguish those services clearly and give visitors enough practical context before they request advice or a quotation.
after.description_2: I structured the content around the main installation routes, project or service proof and direct enquiry actions. Shorter sections make the technical offer easier to scan, while the responsive layout keeps contact and quotation options close to the relevant service.

before.description_1: Envolt needed an electrical services page with a clearer structure and stronger focus. Visitors had to understand the offer quickly, see the practical value and know how to take the next step. The copy also needed to sound more specific and less interchangeable.
before.description_2: I reorganised the page into clear sections that answer the most important visitor questions. The final WordPress page explains the electrical work in plain language, connects benefits to real decisions and keeps contact options visible, making the project easier to read and trust.

after.description_1: Envolt presents electrical and energy services through a focused business website. The portfolio copy needed to explain the actual technical offer and decision path instead of using a sentence accidentally stored in the URL field and generic wording about enquiries.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress experience around the main electrical and energy services, supporting information and clear contact actions. The malformed ACF link was replaced with the project domain, and the content now describes the service journey rather than a generic page-improvement process.

before.description_1: The ozturkmotionpictures website required better wedding information because it was important for people to get the offer before they contacted the company. There was also a need to improve the narrative in terms of structure and wording. Comparing various alternatives meant that people would have to find out quickly what next step to take.
before.description_2: I rebuilt the page around clean sections, clear language, and practical WordPress content modules. The new structure helps visitors understand the project, see the value of the service, and find the next step without friction.

after.description_1: Ozturk Motion Pictures is a wedding-focused visual portfolio built around films, photography, couple stories and galleries. The website needed to let prospective couples understand the style of the work quickly and move naturally from viewing previous weddings to making contact.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress presentation around visual project browsing, concise service context and a clear enquiry route. Large imagery and galleries remain the main proof, while supporting copy helps couples understand what they can request without distracting from the portfolio.

before.description_1: Since the site failed to have accurate information on its pages, it became necessary that essential facts about the property be clearly visible right from the beginning. An effective introduction became important because it could assist in directing users into going through all the sections of the site easily while understanding the offer clearly.
before.description_2: The design for Odetra was improved, with the usage of better English language, but still keeping the content organized. The page contains a clear description of the real estate services provided, no distractions whatsoever, the page allows quick comparison by visitors, and works perfectly on WordPress across all devices.

after.description_1: Odetra presents international real-estate investment and project-development opportunities. The website needed to keep property and market information clear enough for visitors to understand the proposition before moving into company information or direct contact.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress experience around projects, market context and the company proposition, with a clear route from evaluating opportunities to making an enquiry. The content hierarchy keeps property information central and avoids generic claims that could apply to any real-estate website.

before.description_1: It was necessary to narrow down the topics on which Marco Verhuurt could be discussed, since users cannot guess what kind of service the rental project provides. It required clear sections, specific language, and sufficient explanations to build trust without complicating the initial stage of contacting.
before.description_2: The design of the last page focused on clear language, balanced parts, and contact opportunities that come up once there is sufficient background information for the user. It is easier to follow what must be done next in the process of renting, which makes the page more convincing for Marco Verhuurt. Contact used to matter more.

after.description_1: Marco Verhuurt is a rental-focused website where visitors need to understand the available offer, practical conditions and availability before making an enquiry. The portfolio copy therefore needed to describe the rental journey directly instead of speaking generally about page clarity.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience around the rental options, availability and the next contact step. Practical information appears before the enquiry point, giving visitors enough context to decide whether an available option fits their needs.
